text: Now there happened to be there a scoundrel named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He sounded the ram's horn and cried out: "We have no share in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel!"
So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king, all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

When David came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to keep the house and put them under guard. He provided for them, but he did not go in to them. So they were shut away until the day they died, living as widows.
Then the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to me within three days, and be here yourself."
So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time appointed for him.
David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities for himself and escape us."
So Joab's men went out after him, along with the Kerethites and the Pelethites and all the warriors. They left Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

When they reached the great stone at Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic, and strapped over it at his waist was a belt with a sword in its sheath. As he stepped forward, the sword fell out.
Joab said to Amasa, "Are you well, my brother?" And with his right hand Joab took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.

Amasa was not on guard against the sword in Joab's hand, and Joab struck him in the belly with it, spilling his entrails on the ground. He needed no second blow, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
One of Joab's young men stood over Amasa and called out, "Whoever favors Joab and whoever is for David—follow Joab!"

But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him, for everyone who came upon him stopped at the sight.

versions.text: But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him.
versions.explanation: The final clause of the Hebrew verse (כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה כָּל־הַבָּא עָלָיו וְעָמָד, "everyone who came upon him stopped when he saw him") is left untranslated. It explains why the body had to be covered and moved, so its omission loses content.

text: Once he had been removed from the road, all the men went on after Joab in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maacah, and all the Berites gathered together and followed him in.

Joab's forces came and besieged him in Abel Beth Maacah. They threw up a siege ramp against the city, and it stood level with the outer wall, and all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to bring it down.
Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I may speak with him."
He came near, and the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he answered. She said to him, "Listen to the words of your servant." "I am listening," he said.
Then she said, "There was a saying in the old days: 'Let them inquire at Abel'—and so the matter was settled.
I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. Yet you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD's inheritance?"
Joab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!

That is not the case. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Hand over that one man, and I will withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you over the wall."

Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He sounded the ram's horn, and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own tent. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites;
Adoram was in charge of forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the record keeper;
Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
and Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.
